company_description: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a cruise company in North America, Europe, the Asia-Pacific, and internationally. It offers itineraries to destinations, such as Europe, Asia, Australia, New Zealand, South America, Africa, Canada, Bermuda, the Caribbean, and Alaska; and inter-island itinerary in Hawaii. The company also provides features, amenities, and activities, including various accommodations, dining venues, bars and lounges, spas, casino and retail shopping areas, and entertainment choices; shore excursions at each port of call, and air transportation and hotel packages for stays before or after a voyage. It offers its products and services under the Norwegian Cruise Line, Oceania Cruises, and Regent Seven Seas Cruises brands. The company was founded in 1966 and is based in Miami, Florida.

risks.title: Interest Rate Risk on Variable Rate Debt
risks.summary: The company is exposed to rising interest rates on its variable rate debt, which could significantly increase its annual interest expenses.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Item 7A. As of December 31, 2025, 10% of debt was at variable rates (compared to 6% in 2024). A 1% increase in SOFR rates would increase annual interest expenses by approximately $15 million. The language is factual and quantified. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Foreign Exchange Risk on Shipbuilding Contracts
risks.summary: Euro-denominated shipbuilding contracts expose the company to significant exchange rate volatility, with potential impacts of several billion dollars on future payment obligations.
risks.score_rationale: Described in Item 7A. Unhedged payments on shipbuilding contracts amount to €16.4 billion or $19.3 billion at the December 31, 2025 exchange rate. A 10% change in the euro would result in an approximate impact of $1.93 billion. The language is precise and quantified. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Holding Structure Dependence for Distributions

risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Item 7. NCLH is a holding company that depends on its subsidiaries to receive distributions to fund its obligations. Existing debt agreements limit subsidiaries' ability to pay dividends. (default score, to be refined)
